Q1: Acephate presents significant known hazards, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, or reproductive toxicity (CMR1), environmental toxicity (ENV1), oral toxicity (ORL1), and organ/systemic toxicity (OGN1), all recognized under GHS. Beyond GHS, it shows potential endocrine disruption (EDC2) and dermal/eye hazards (SKN2) based on expanded scientific data. Conversely, inhalation hazards are considered low to moderate (IHL3) due to supporting studies.
Q2: Acephate is listed by the EPA as a Pesticide Active Ingredient and appears on the Safe Drinking Water Act Contaminant Candidate List, indicating potential environmental and health concerns. It is also identified on the TEDX list of potential endocrine disruptors.
Q3: Acephate is very well characterized, with over 6,000 literature references and 234 toxicity records, placing it among the most studied chemicals in our database. Its hazard profile is considered comprehensive, featuring a well-defined molecular structure, no data-deficient hazard tiers, and formal evaluation by the EPA's rigorous IRIS program.
